events.name: Sacramento River, near Rio Vista, California
events.blurb: Humpback filmed about 60 miles up the Sacramento River.
events.summary: A humpback whale was filmed about 60 miles (97 km) up the Sacramento River near Rio Vista on Sept. 16, 2026, after entering San Francisco Bay earlier that week. Its most recent documented sighting before this was in Baja California in February (per the Marine Mammal Center). Its sex is unknown.

events.name: Sacramento River, up to the Port of Sacramento
events.blurb: Mother and calf (Delta and Dawn) reached the Port of Sacramento, about 90 miles inland.
events.summary: A mother and calf nicknamed Delta and Dawn were first spotted in the Sacramento River on May 13, 2007 and travelled about 90 miles inland to the Port of Sacramento. Both had wounds consistent with a boat strike. They spent nearly three weeks in the Delta, circling near the Rio Vista bridge for several days, before returning to the Pacific.

events.name: San Francisco Bay, near Candlestick Park
events.blurb: Humphrey returned and stranded on a mudflat near Candlestick Park.
events.summary: Five years after his first visit, the humpback nicknamed Humphrey returned to San Francisco Bay and stranded on a mudflat near Candlestick Park. Rescuers pulled him off with a large cargo net and a Coast Guard boat and guided him back toward the Pacific.

events.name: Sacramento River, past Rio Vista (dead-end slough)
events.blurb: Humphrey swam about 69 miles up the Sacramento River to a dead-end slough.
events.summary: A humpback nicknamed Humphrey was first spotted at Oakland's Outer Harbor on Oct. 10, 1985. He swam up the Carquinez Strait and the Sacramento River, under the Rio Vista Bridge, to a dead-end slough about 69 miles (111 km) from the ocean. He spent about 25 days in the bay and delta before rescuers guided him back to the Pacific using recorded whale sounds.
